name: USB RFID Reader/Writer DL533N
one_line: USB-stick 13.56MHz LibNFC-compatible reader/writer that reads, writes, dumps and emulates MIFARE/NFC HF cards from a PC.
why_notable: Low-cost USB-tethered HF RFID read/write/crack tool, a different form factor from standalone devices like the Proxmark or ACR122U.

name: PN532Killer
one_line: Standalone AD156-based board that reads, emulates and sniffs ISO14443A/B, ISO15693 and EM4100 over UART, incl. nested/hardnested MIFARE key recovery.
why_notable: 47 stars, last commit 2026-01-02. Price from a cached MTools Tec listing - live store page returned 403, so treat as medium confidence.

name: NFC Card Reader Module with ESP32-S3
one_line: ESP32-S3 + PN5321 module reading, writing and emulating ISO14443 A/B, MIFARE and FeliCa, with an 8-LED array, 3W speaker and microSD for audio-visual feedback on tag events.
why_notable: Full read/write/emulate NFC chipset on an ESP32-S3, though the listing frames it as an access-control project board rather than a pentest tool.

name: GGtag
one_line: RP2040 e-paper badge emulating 125kHz RFID tags (ASK and FSK), programmed over USB serial, a web-serial browser interface, or audio via ggwave; 3.52-inch e-paper display.
why_notable: Novel form factor for RFID tag emulation - not a Proxmark/Chameleon/Flipper-style reader.

name: ESP-RFID-Tool v2 PRO
one_line: ESP-based Wiegand logging/testing/replay tool for card readers: captures raw Wiegand, computes UIDs in 26/34/35/56-bit formats, replays captures, fuzzes and brute-forces access-control panels.
why_notable: 29 stars, last commit 2026-08-25. EUR38 converted. Distinct vendor and hardware from ESPKey and the original ESP RFID Tool.

name: VICINO
one_line: ST25R3916B RFID/NFC reader-writer module over SPI, pin- and mounting-hole-compatible with existing RC522 project designs.
why_notable: Higher-end RFID chipset than the common cheap MFRC522 boards, positioned as a drop-in upgrade.

name: RFIDler
one_line: Standalone PIC32MX795F512L software-defined LF (125/134kHz) reader/writer/emulator covering EM4100, HID Prox, Indala and other LF formats via USB CLI.
why_notable: ~485 stars, last commit 2024-09-22. Early and widely cited open LF RFID SDR platform; current retail availability uncertain.

name: Wiegotcha
one_line: Raspberry Pi 3 covert long-range badge-capture rig built to hide inside a Maxiprox 5375, Indala ASR-620 or HID R90 and log Wiegand data over Wi-Fi; needs a donor reader.
why_notable: 239 stars, last commit 2021-10-25. Kept past the staleness cutoff as the widely-cited reference build for covert long-range Wiegand interception.

name: Gatekeeper
one_line: Raspberry Pi 3 + Proxmark3 rig derived from Wiegotcha that hides in a long-range HID reader, captures badge data and clones to a blank card in the field via web UI.
why_notable: 19 stars, last commit 2024-04-16. Adds same-session cloning to the Wiegotcha design.

name: 7941W RFID Card Cloner
one_line: Handheld dual-frequency (125kHz + 13.56MHz) cloner from a Seeed XIAO nRF52840, a 7941W reader/writer module, an 8x8 LED matrix and a joystick.
why_notable: 6 stars, last commit 2024-03-12, repo archived by the author. Full documented BOM.

name: RFID Field Detector Ultra - LF/HF/UHF
one_line: Passive, battery-free tri-band (LF/HF/UHF) detector that lights up to indicate the presence of an active RFID reader field.
why_notable: Covers all three RFID frequency bands in one passive field-presence detector, useful for locating hidden readers during a physical audit.

name: Flipper Add-On: MagSpoof
one_line: Flipper Zero GPIO add-on board implementing the MagSpoof magnetic-stripe emulator/spoofer technique.
why_notable: Flipper-specific hardware implementation of the MagSpoof magstripe-emulation technique already tracked as a standalone device elsewhere.

name: Proxmark 3 RDV4 - SIM/SAM Extension
one_line: SIM/SAM card slot extension module for the Proxmark 3 RDV4, enabling smart-card cryptographic operations.
why_notable: Capability-adding accessory for the already-tracked Proxmark3 RDV4.01, adding smart-card crypto support.

name: Cypher NFC (cypher-pn532)
one_line: DIY handheld NFC workstation (ESP32-C3 + PN532 + SSD1306 OLED + SD) that dumps/clones MIFARE Classic and NTAG, runs dictionary key attacks and emulates NDEF tags.
why_notable: 48 stars, last commit 2026-08-08. Schematics and PCB files published; ports to M5Stack Cardputer ADV.

name: RFID Detector / Diagnostic Card v2
one_line: Credit-card-sized detector with LEDs that light up to indicate the presence and frequency band (125kHz/13.56MHz/860-960MHz) of a nearby RFID reader.
why_notable: An active RFID-reader-detection tool, a different function from the cloning/emulation tools already tracked.

name: RFID HF Field Generator
one_line: Coin-cell-powered 13.56MHz field generator used to power passive HF RFID/NFC tags and implants without a reader present.
why_notable: Borderline because its documented use is powering RFID implants/tags rather than directly attacking a target system.

name: ARD RFID Blocker (Pack of 2) - NFC Blocker
one_line: Credit-card-sized, battery-free active RFID/NFC jammer that blocks reads of cards placed above or below it, unlike passive faraday-sleeve wallets.
why_notable: Active jamming device rather than a passive shield, a distinct defensive capability from typical RFID-blocking wallets/sleeves.
